exclusions: All 14 canonical identities, active placement-specific rejects and every untriggered PARKED revisit were excluded. Exact identities and primary discovery lanes retained in Runs 53–74 were not recycled.
The protected internal handoffs Transparency → When We Froze and When We Froze → Stardancer remain unavailable; Truth in Noise → Transparency and every other boundary remain available.
No lead was promoted for recency, reputation, genre, novelty, title or technical cleverness. Release-level claims were not converted into exact-track behaviour.

Energy, density, space, hypnosis, emotional effect, phrase structure, harmonic relation, perceived pulse and mixability remain unknown. Descriptions of metre, syncopation and transformation are evidence, not flow verdicts.
rankedLeadSummary: 1. Jump Source — A Dull Knife ft. Harmony Index: strongest current transformation, moving from a dub-techno groove into a vocal-led syncopated bass construction.
2. Cabasa — Intentional Drowning: strongest overlooked polyrhythmic lead, documented as seven minutes balanced between danceable and undanceable.
3. Cassegrain — Plate#2: strongest overlooked syncopated-techno lead, riding an uneven, sharply syncopated rhythm.
4. Drums Off Chaos — Clockwise Instinct: strongest adjacent metre-specific construction, explicitly looping in groups of seven.
